title: Sliced Pd/Bs — approximate patch and estimated MIDI
method: Spectrogram and FFT inspection identify broad opening Eb4/F4/Bb4 families, then Db4/F4/Bb4 and lower chord movements. Repeated RMS rises give a pulse interval near 112 ms. This MIDI approximates the audible sliced output with a short-short-long gate pattern and three-note voicings, with the software arpeggiator disabled. It does not reconstruct the original held chords, split allocation, or factory rhythm grid.
uncertainties: Original performance MIDI and recording-specific factory SysEx are unavailable. This is an estimated audio reconstruction, not an exact original performance or authenticated factory patch.
Every note-on velocity is fixed to 100 as an explicit unknown placeholder; note-off velocity is 64. These values were not recovered from the audio.
Played-key octave and voicing are conditional on the newly designed patch. The hardware oscillator tuning, system transpose, original key presses, controller changes, and effect history are unknown.
Onsets refer to the decoded public MP3. MP3 encoder delay, hardware latency, recording processing, exact gates, and release tails are not recovered.
The strong detune and overlapping voices make exact chord voicing uncertain. Some apparent lower notes could be separate split bass notes rather than the three-note chords used here.
The short-short-long rhythm is an explicit approximation of prominent pulse groups; quieter subdivisions and ties may differ.
This MIDI describes estimated sliced output, not original key presses. It will not verify the fidelity of the software arpeggiator or original patch rhythm.
No original note-on velocity, controller motion, patch split point, or exact oscillator settings were recovered.

patch_design.name: APX Sliced
rationale: Broad paired Super Saw voices approximate the thick, detuned harmonic bands.
The short amplitude release supports the explicit estimated MIDI slicing.
A lower cutoff and smaller filter contour reduce excessive upper harmonics in the first software preview. A stronger modulated delay adds stereo spread toward the wide hardware recording.
uncertainties: These are newly designed software parameters informed by the public demo, not recovered Roland factory settings.
No authentic factory dump or controlled hardware measurements exist for this comparison.

The factory patch may use a split bass/pad arrangement or an internal gated arpeggiator. This approximation uses one polyphonic tone driven by direct output MIDI and therefore does not establish the original patch topology.
This approximate patch was revised after comparing a software preview with the MP3; its selected values are manual voicing choices, not recovered hardware parameters.

voicing_review.basis: Original MP3 versus initial software render: whole-excerpt power spectrum and stereo side-to-mid energy. Changes affect only this approximate patch; no DSP changes or recovered factory parameter claims.
voicing_review.method: A bounded manual review reduced obvious brightness and stereo-width mismatches. Spectral centroid is descriptive and does not establish perceptual or hardware equivalence.
voicing_review.limitations: The unknown original patch and estimated MIDI prevent identifying a unique parameter solution. Remaining temporal, spectral and stereo differences are expected.
